title: Cup height entered infants' looking around seven and a half months
summary: Only the 7.5-month group, in a series that also tested 5.5 and 6.5 months, dwelt on a tall object vanishing inside a squat cup.
body: Later in the same 2002 review, Baillargeon and Wang describe the cup version given to three older ages. Five-and-a-half months and six-and-a-half months did not single out the impossible hiding. Seven and a half months did. The review's conclusion is that containment is when infants start to use how tall the cup is, relative to the object, to predict whether the object can vanish inside it. The review also mentions, from unpublished work, that a cover lowered over an object was later still, near 12 months. That cover result is not this claim. Ages here are the tested groups.

sources.title: Event categorization in infancy
sources.author: Renée Baillargeon and Su-hua Wang
sources.note: Peer-reviewed Trends in Cognitive Sciences review, 1 February 2002, PMC4215955. Paraphrase of the 7.5-month containment-height result.
